equationblock.title: Rate law you keep forgetting
equationblock.caption: The Arrhenius equation, higher temperature, exponentially faster rate.

steps.label: Subtract 3 from both sides
steps.why: Undo the +3 to isolate the x-term.

steps.label: Divide both sides by 2
steps.why: Undo the ×2 to leave x alone.

quiz.title: Quick check
quiz.question: Which reaction order has a half-life independent of concentration?

options.feedback: Right, first-order half-life is ln2/k, with no [A].

quiz.explanation: Only first-order kinetics gives a constant half-life regardless of starting amount.

flashcard.title: Interval ear-training deck

cards.back: Sounds like: "Twinkle Twinkle" opening. 7 semitones. The power chord of classical harmony.
Sounds like: "When the Saints Go Marching In." 4 semitones. Defines a major chord.
Sounds like: "Smoke on the Water" riff. 3 semitones. Defines a minor chord, darker colour.
Sounds like: "Somewhere Over the Rainbow" opening leap. 12 semitones. Same note, doubled frequency.
The Devil's interval, 6 semitones, right in the middle of the octave. Unstable; resolves inward to a 3rd or outward to a 6th.

flashcard.footer: Flip each card after singing the interval. Aim for instant recognition, the goal is hearing, not counting semitones.

periodictable.title: The elements in your reaction
periodictable.footer: The highlighted elements are the ones in this week’s mechanisms.

bodymap.title: Primary muscles worked, marathon training
bodymap.footer: Quads do the heavy lifting; calves absorb impact on every stride.

geometrycanvas.title: A 30-60-90 triangle
geometrycanvas.footer: The 30-60-90 triangle: sides scale as 1 : √3 : 2. Memorise the short side and derive the rest.

freebodydiagram.title: Forces on a sliding block
freebodydiagram.footer: Net horizontal force = 12 − 5 = 7 N → acceleration = 0.35 m/s² rightward.

musicstaff.title: C major scale (treble clef)
musicstaff.footer: C major uses only white keys, no sharps or flats. Every other major scale is this same pattern of whole and half steps (W W H W W W H) transposed to a new root.

vectorspace.title: Eigenvectors of a 2×2 matrix
vectorspace.footer: Solid = original eigenvector, dashed = transformed. v₁ stretches (λ=3); v₂ is unchanged (λ=1).

reactionmechanism.title: SN2 Mechanism: methyl bromide + OH⁻
reactionmechanism.footer: One step, backside attack, inversion of configuration (Walden inversion). Second-order: rate = k[CH₃Br][OH⁻].

milestones.label: Points to show interest (not just to request)

teachdiagram.title: Pythagorean theorem, built step by step

steps.caption: Draw a right triangle with legs a and b.
The hypotenuse c runs from the top corner to the right corner.

gridmatrix.title: Ten-Frame: Showing 7
gridmatrix.note: 7 filled dots, 3 empty — a quick way to see how far a number is from 10.

fractionbar.title: Comparing Fractions
fractionbar.note: ¾ is the largest of the three; ½ is the smallest.

wave.title: Wavelength and amplitude of a sound wave
wave.footer: At 343 m/s in air, a 440 Hz tone has wavelength λ = v/f = 343/440 ≈ 0.78 m. The 2nd harmonic (880 Hz) has half the wavelength and, here, half the amplitude.

energydiagram.title: Energy profile of an exothermic reaction
energydiagram.footer: Ea = 75 kJ/mol is the barrier the reactants must overcome; the products sit 45 kJ/mol lower, so ΔH = −45 kJ/mol — energy is released (exothermic). A catalyst would lower the peak (smaller Ea) without changing ΔH.

phylotree.title: How the great apes are related
phylotree.footer: Each branch point is a common ancestor. Chimpanzees and bonobos are each other’s closest relatives, and together they are humans’ closest living kin.

parsetree.title: Grammar: a constituency parse tree
parsetree.sentence: The quick fox jumps over the lazy dog.
parsetree.footer: The sentence (S) splits into a noun phrase (NP) and a verb phrase (VP); the VP nests a prepositional phrase (PP) that carries its own NP.

celldiagram.title: Anatomy of an animal cell

parts.note: Selectively permeable boundary controlling what enters and leaves.
Gel-like fluid where the organelles sit and most reactions occur.
Holds the DNA and directs the cell; the nucleolus inside builds ribosomes.
The powerhouse: makes ATP via aerobic respiration.
Endoplasmic reticulum — folds and transports proteins and lipids.
Golgi apparatus — packages and ships processed proteins.
Sites of protein synthesis (translate mRNA into polypeptides).

celldiagram.footer: An animal cell has no cell wall, chloroplasts, or large central vacuole — those are plant-cell features.

raydiagram.title: Convex lens: object beyond 2F
raydiagram.footer: With d<sub>o</sub> = 30 cm and f = 10 cm, the lens equation gives d<sub>i</sub> = 15 cm: a real, inverted image at half size (m = −0.5). This is how a camera forms its picture.

vectorfield.title: Slope field for y' = x − y
vectorfield.footer: Each dash is the tangent slope x − y at that point; the solution curve flows along them, settling toward the line y = x − 1.

pedigree.title: Tracing an autosomal recessive trait
pedigree.footer: Both grandparents (I-1, I-2) are unaffected carriers (Aa), so each child had a 1-in-4 chance of being affected (aa). The proband II-2 is affected; the trait skips a generation — the hallmark of autosomal recessive inheritance.

bohrmodel.title: Bohr model of a sodium atom
bohrmodel.name: Sodium
bohrmodel.footer: Sodium has 11 protons, so a neutral atom has 11 electrons arranged 2·8·1 across three shells. That single electron in the outer (n3) shell is easily lost — which is why sodium readily forms the Na⁺ ion.

equationbalancer.title: Combustion of methane
equationbalancer.caption: CH₄ + 2 O₂ → CO₂ + 2 H₂O. Every element has the same number of atoms on each side, so mass is conserved and the equation is balanced.
equationbalancer.footer: The coefficient of 2 on O₂ supplies the 4 oxygen atoms the products need (2 in CO₂ + 2 in the two H₂O molecules), while 2 H₂O accounts for all 4 hydrogens from methane.

yieldcalc.title: Percent yield: ammonia synthesis
yieldcalc.footer: Each mole of N₂ needs 3 mol H₂ — 2.0 mol N₂ would need 6.0 mol H₂, but only 5.0 mol is on hand, so H₂ caps the reaction at 3.33 mol NH₃ (56.8 g theoretical). Recovering 42.5 g in the lab is a 74.8% yield.

vseprmolecule.title: Shape of a water molecule
vseprmolecule.caption: Oxygen has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs. The four electron domains repel into a tetrahedral arrangement, but only the two O–H bonds are visible — giving water its bent shape.
vseprmolecule.footer: The two lone pairs sit closer to the oxygen and push the O–H bonds together, compressing the angle from the ideal tetrahedral 109.5° down to 104.5°. This bent, polar geometry is why water is such a good solvent.

unitcircle.title: Unit circle at θ = 135°
unitcircle.caption: At 135° (3π/4 radians) the terminal point is (−√2/2, √2/2): cosine is negative and sine is positive, placing it in the second quadrant.
unitcircle.footer: 135° has a reference angle of 45°, so its sine and cosine share the magnitude √2/2 ≈ 0.707 — only the cosine flips sign because the radius now points up and to the left.

solidfigure.title: Rectangular prism
solidfigure.caption: A 5 × 4 × 3 cm box. Surface area sums the six rectangular faces (2(lw + lh + wh) = 94 cm²) and volume is l × w × h = 60 cm³.
solidfigure.footer: Every convex solid satisfies Euler’s formula V − E + F = 2: here 8 − 12 + 6 = 2, a quick check that the vertex, edge and face counts are consistent.

crosssection.title: Inside the Earth
crosssection.caption: The Earth is layered by density: a thin rocky crust over the deep mantle, then a liquid iron-nickel outer core and a solid inner core at the centre.
crosssection.footer: Convection in the liquid outer core generates Earth’s magnetic field, while the immense pressure at the centre keeps the inner core solid despite temperatures near 5,200 °C.

pianokeys.title: C major 7 chord
pianokeys.caption: A major-7 stacks a major triad with a major 7th: C–E–G–B.
pianokeys.footer: The bright, jazzy colour comes from that major-7th interval (B over C) — a half-step below the octave.

fretboardmap.title: A minor pentatonic
fretboardmap.caption: The box-1 shape at the 5th fret — roots on the low E, D, and high E strings anchor the position.

circleoffifths.title: Circle of fifths
circleoffifths.caption: G major sits one sharp clockwise of C: its IV is C, its V is D, and Em is its relative minor.

odontogram.title: Adult dental chart
odontogram.caption: Universal numbering: teeth 1–16 across the upper arch, 17–32 across the lower.

clockface.title: Reading the clock
clockface.caption: The hour hand sits past 3, two-thirds of the way toward 4, while the minute hand points to the 8 — forty minutes past the hour.

moneytray.title: Counting coins
moneytray.caption: Three quarters make 75¢, two dimes add 20¢, and four pennies add 4¢ — ninety-nine cents in all.

placevaluechart.title: Place value of 347
placevaluechart.caption: Each digit holds a different value by its place: 3 hundreds, 4 tens, and 7 ones combine to make 347.

shapecard.title: Shapes and their attributes
shapecard.caption: A hexagon is a flat six-sided polygon; a cube is the solid you get when six square faces meet at eight corners.

letterform.title: Forming lowercase 'a'

strokes.hint: Start below the midline and curve left, down, and around to close the bowl.
Draw a straight line down the right side, sitting on the baseline.

letterform.caption: The lowercase a is built from two strokes: a round bowl, then a straight tail on the right.

toolscale.title: Reading a ruler
toolscale.caption: The arrow lands three of the eight marks past the 2-inch line, which reads 2 and three-eighths inches.

craftchart.title: Cross-stitch heart motif
craftchart.caption: Work each ×: bring the needle up at the bottom-left of the square and down at the top-right, then cross back the other way. Count stitches along the top, rows down the right.

areamodel.title: 23 × 14 area model
areamodel.caption: Each cell shows the partial product; the sum equals 322.

pyramidtiers.title: Bloom's taxonomy

tiers.label: Understand
tiers.note: Explain ideas in your own words

tiers.label: Apply
tiers.note: Use the concept in a new situation

tiers.label: Evaluate
tiers.note: Justify a decision or course of action

tiers.label: Create
tiers.note: Produce something new using learned skills

pyramidtiers.caption: Higher tiers require deeper cognitive engagement. Most exam questions test Apply and above.

linespectrum.title: Hydrogen emission spectrum (Balmer series)
linespectrum.caption: Each line corresponds to an electron falling to n=2. The 656 nm red Hα line is brightest.

dnahelix.title: DNA — Watson-Crick base pairing
dnahelix.caption: A-T (2 H-bonds) and G-C (3 H-bonds) pair across the two antiparallel strands.

columnarithmetic.title: Adding with regrouping: 267 + 458
columnarithmetic.caption: 7 + 8 makes 15 — write the 5, carry the 1. That carried 1 joins the tens column, and 6 + 5 + 1 carries again into the hundreds.

titrationcurve.title: Titrating acetic acid with NaOH
titrationcurve.footer: The flat buffer region runs where acetic acid and its conjugate base coexist; the steep jump near 25 mL marks the equivalence point, and the curve sits basic there (pH 8.72) because acetate is a weak base.

interferencepattern.title: Double-slit interference of green laser light
interferencepattern.footer: The bright fringes fall where the path difference from the two slits is a whole number of wavelengths; the envelope tapers off toward the edges of the screen.

orbitaldiagram.title: Electron configuration of iron
orbitaldiagram.footer: Hund's rule fills all five 3d boxes singly before any pairs up — so the sixth 3d electron is the only paired one, leaving four unpaired electrons overall.

pictograph.title: Population by continent
pictograph.footer: Each icon stands for 500 million people, so Asia’s roughly 4.7 billion tiles as nine full icons plus a sliver.

particlemodel.title: Particle arrangement across the three phases
particlemodel.footer: Same particle count, three arrangements: a solid locks particles into a rigid grid, a liquid keeps them touching but mobile, and a gas lets them spread across the whole container.

morphemebreakdown.title: Breaking down "unbreakable"

morphemes.meaning: to separate into pieces by force

morphemebreakdown.footer: The prefix negates the root and the suffix turns it into an adjective: "not able to be broken."

sessions.note: Tempo still rushes in the climax

taxonrank.title: Where T. rex fits in the tree of life
taxonrank.footer: Every rung down the ladder gets more specific — "Animalia" fits every animal ever, "T. rex" fits exactly one.

numbersequence.title: The Fibonacci sequence
numbersequence.rule: Each term is the sum of the two terms before it.

constantcard.title: Pi
constantcard.significance: The ratio of a circle’s circumference to its diameter — the same for every circle, no matter the size, and it never repeats or terminates.

elementcard.title: Element deep dive: oxygen
elementcard.name: Oxygen
elementcard.footer: The same O that anchors carbon dioxide and water anchors half of Earth’s crust by mass.

energybarchart.title: Energy of a swinging pendulum
energybarchart.footer: With no friction, total mechanical energy stays 100 J — it just shifts between gravitational (Ug) and kinetic (KE).

guitartab.title: A minor pentatonic run
guitartab.footer: The A minor pentatonic 'box' shape, ascending from the low E string. Note the h (hammer-on) and b (bend) markings.

karyotype.title: Human karyotype — Trisomy 21
karyotype.footer: A karyogram arranges the 46 chromosomes into 23 pairs. Three copies of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21) underlies Down syndrome.

frayermodel.title: Vocabulary — Photosynthesis
frayermodel.definition: The process green plants and algae use to turn sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose (food) and oxygen.
examples: A fern growing in a shady forest
A tomato plant on a windowsill
nonexamples: Rust forming on an iron nail
frayermodel.footer: Non-examples sharpen the boundary: they may involve energy or gases, but none build sugar from light.

numberbond.title: Number bond for 10
numberbond.label: Six and four make ten
numberbond.footer: Number bonds show how a whole splits into parts — the foundation of addition and subtraction fact families.
